statements.statement: Abstraction means you must understand every internal detail before you can use something.
statements.explanation: Abstraction is the opposite, it means hiding details you don't need. You can drive a car without understanding how the pistons work, just as programmers use tools without knowing every internal mechanism.

statements.statement: When a programmer names a complex piece of logic 'send_email,' they are using abstraction.
statements.explanation: By tucking the complicated steps of sending an email behind a simple name, the programmer hides the details. Anyone using 'send_email' doesn't need to know how it works internally.

statements.statement: Abstraction makes programs harder to understand because it removes information.
statements.explanation: Abstraction actually makes programs easier to understand. By hiding unnecessary details behind simple names, programmers can focus on the big picture without getting lost in complexity.
